chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Kumaydani narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Four people must perform complete prayers whether they are traveling or at home: the renter of beasts of burden, the driver of the rented beasts, the courier, and the shepherd, because it is their work. The compiler of this book said: The courier refers to the postman.

key_terms.التِّمَامُ: Complete prayers (performing all four rak'ahs instead of two)

ai.seo_question: Who are the four people required to perform complete prayers while traveling according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* establishes that individuals engaged in continuous, duty-bound professions—specifically animal renters, drivers, couriers (al-Ishtiqan), and shepherds—must perform complete prayers (tamam) rather than shortening them (qasr) during travel. The ruling is grounded in the principle that their work constitutes a form of continuous presence or specific obligation that precludes the legal status of a traveler entitled to qasr, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the nature of one's activity over mere geographical distance.
